newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BLUE JAYS' HENTGEN WINS AMERICAN LEAGUE CY YOUNG AWARD. [CORRECTED 23:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BLUE JAYS' HENTGEN WINS AMERICAN LEAGUE CY YOUNG AWARD. [CORRECTED 23:55 GMT]

text.p: Toronto Blue Jays pitcher Pat Hentgen handed the New York Yankees their first loss in the post-season awards on Tuesday, edging Andy Pettitte by six points for the American League Cy Young Award.

Hentgen received 16 of 28 first-place votes, nine seconds and three thirds for 110 points in balloting by the Baseball Writers' Association of America. Pettitte picked up 11 first-place votes, 16 seconds and one third for 104 points.
Two voters from each A.L. city selected their top three choices, with five points awarded for first, three for second and one for third.

Hentgen, who turns 28 Wednesday, went 20-10 (corrects from 20-8) to post more than one-fourth of Toronto's 74 victories. He led the majors in innings pitched (265 2/3) and complete games (10), and his 3.22 ERA ranked second in the A.L. behind teammate Juan Guzman.

The right-hander posted career highs in wins and earned run average in his fifth big-league season. His previous bests came in 1993, when he went 19-9 with a 3.87 ERA for the eventual World Series champion Blue Jays.

The 24-year-old Pettitte was 21-8 with a 3.87 ERA during the regular season. He led the A.L. in victories in only his second big-league season. Pettitte went 12-9 with a 4.17 ERA last year to finish third in Rookie of the Year balloting.

The young lefty figured to be the number three starter in the Yankees' rotation coming out of spring training. But as veterans fell by the wayside due to injury or ineffectiveness Pettitte stepped up to become the New York stopper.
He was 13-3 following Yankee losses during the regular season and pitched eight shutout innings in Game 5 to help lift the Yankees to the World Series title.

The Yankees were hoping to continue their sweep of the American League post-season awards after shortstop Derek Jeter (Rookie of the Year) and Joe Torre (Manager of the Year) took home awards last week.

Pettitte's teammate, setup man Mariano Rivera, received the final first-place vote and placed third with 18 points. The 26-year-old Rivera went 8-3 with a 2.09 ERA and picked up six saves when filling in for an injured John Wetteland in the closer's role.

Charles Nagy of the Cleveland Indians finished fourth with 12 points and Baltimore's Mike Mussina was fifth (5), followed by Alex Fernandez (1) and Roberto Hernandez (1) of the Chicago White Sox and Ken Hill of the Texas Rangers (1).

Nagy went 17-5 with a 3.41 ERA for the Central Division champs. Mussina posted an impressive 19-11 mark, but had a 4.81 ERA and failed in four chances for his 20th win. Fernandez was 16-10 with a 3.45 ERA, while Hernandez recorded 38 saves and a 1.91 ERA. Hill was 16-10 with a 3.63 ERA.
Atlanta's John Smoltz was named the National League Cy Young Award winner on Monday. The N.L. Most Valuable Player will be announced Wednesday and the A.L. MVP will be named on Thursday.
